flags.why: Quan tài is used nationwide, so Northern incorrectly restricts its use ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/quan-tai-empQRRu7fsFkC.html)).
In physics, lực means force, whereas power is a different physical quantity ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/l%E1%BB%B1c)).
The entry omits the ordinary meaning strength, restricting lực to physics ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/l%E1%BB%B1c)).
flags.fix: noun | strength; physical power — Cú đá này có lực rất mạnh. = This kick is very powerful.

flags.why: Everyday colloquial soi also means scrutinizing someone's affairs or appearance, without an optical instrument ([usage](https://tuoitre.vn/plo/thong-tin-soi-doi-tu-ky-thi-nguoi-dong-tinh-post38800.html)).
flags.fix: verb [colloquial] | to scrutinize; to pry into — Đừng soi đời tư của người khác. = Don't pry into other people's private lives.

flags.why: In this example, xô describes displacement out of position rather than an action of pushing something over ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-x%C3%B4)).
flags.fix: to shift out of position; to become displaced
